- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.3) and price is trending up, model frequently underestimates the continuation; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture momentum.
- Model tends to lag in mean reversion periods — when price is above 30-day moving average, forecast often stays above; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- In early horizon (e.g., 3–5 days ahead), model often underestimates volatility; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- When sentiment is high and price is near support, model often fails to anticipate reversal; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overbought bias.
- If sentiment is low and price is near resistance, model often overreacts; cap forecast at 1–2% below prior peak to avoid false breakout.
